collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 6-13; in the story (name1) is deaf and (his/her) household signs at home)

collection.description: A child eats for the first time with a deaf villager's family, who all sign at dinner: teach them a sign, or let them just watch.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At (subject)'s fire, dinner is noisy in two ways at once: half the family talks and signs, the other half just signs, and everybody's hands are going between bites. Tonight (friend), a friend of the youngest child, has come to eat for the first time, and is sitting very still with (friend.his/her) bowl, completely lost.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) catches (friend)'s eye and slowly shows (friend.him/her) the sign for "fish," then "please," then "more." (friend) copies. The whole family cheers silently, which mostly involves waving. By the end of the meal (friend) can ask for fish, say thank you, and say "that's disgusting," which the youngest child taught (friend.him/her) when no one was looking.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) eats and watches. Hands fly back and forth. Faces do a lot of the talking. (friend.He/she) understands more than (friend.he/she) expected: that the smallest child has been in trouble, that (subject) thinks the stew is too salty, that somebody just made a joke about somebody else's hat. On the way home (friend.he/she) practices the hat joke on (friend.his/her) own fingers.
